original_question: Which type of MPS-III Sanfilippo syndrome is caused by a mutation in the gene that encodes an enzyme responsible for degrading heparan sulfate by hydrolyzing terminal N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residues in N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminides?

final_qi.question: Which type of MPS-III Sanfilippo syndrome is caused by a mutation in the gene that encodes an enzyme responsible for degrading heparan sulfate by hydrolyzing terminal N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residues in N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminides?
final_qi.long_answer: Sanfilippo syndrome type B (MPS IIIB) results from mutations in the NAGLU gene, which encodes α-N-acetylglucosaminidase. This lysosomal hydrolase normally degrades heparan sulfate by cleaving terminal N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residues from N-acetyl-α-D-glucosaminides; loss of its function causes the accumulation of heparan sulfate characteristic of MPS-III type B.
